title: Worker-persistent state outlives the request that owns it: producer → missed reset → release → early consumer
index_line: T-0015 · MEM_WRITE · worker-global slot still points into a freed request heap; a consumer that runs before normal init acts on it · php/python/node/ruby · corroborated
invariant_violated: A multi-request worker assumes teardown and re-initialisation are one atomic step: whatever the previous request published into worker-global state is assumed gone before the next request runs. The gap between 'request heap freed' and 'global state reset' is reachable, and nothing in the request lifecycle says so.

mechanism.does: a request drives an operation that publishes request-owned state into a slot the worker keeps across requests (here: session/decoder/error state from multipart upload progress)
an interruption abandons the operation before its matching reset runs
the worker frees the request heap while the worker-global field still refers into it
a LATER request, same worker, reaches an operation that runs before normal request initialisation (INI diagnostics before request startup
that operation reads, frees or branches on the stale value and treats it as valid state
a groomed heap layout places attacker-chosen data where the stale pointer is dereferenced, turning the read into a controlled call

source.http.request.value: the multipart/upload request that is simultaneously producer and consumer — no application code and no session_start() needed; an interruption after state is published plus one later request on the same worker is the whole requirement

lifetime.object.value: the alloc → abort → free → reuse triangle spanning a request boundary: the record's owner (the request) dies, the reference (the worker global) does not

size.length.value: memory_limit / body / timeout sizing is the cheapest deterministic interrupt, and OOM is the application-independent trigger — it produces the abort, it is not the bug

guard.none.value: no boundary guard exists; the fix resets wider state precisely because no configuration option covers every producer/consumer pair

preconditions.expr: a persistent (multi-request) worker serves the traffic, so a global can outlive its request
the early consumer exists in config: session.upload_progress on (default) or early INI diagnostics before request startup
build is inside the affected range (PHP < 8.2.35 / 8.3.36 / 8.4.27 / 8.5.12; sibling CVE-2026-109618 fixed in the same releases)

check.spec: php -r 'echo PHP_VERSION;' # then compare against 8.2.35 / 8.3.36 / 8.4.27 / 8.5.12 — anything lower is in range

preconditions.expr: the attacker can open two requests that land on the same worker (connection reuse, pinned session, or enough concurrency to hit a pool child twice)

check.spec: profile the pool: static pm.max_children=1 pins one worker (deterministic); dynamic pins nothing (retry the producer/consumer pair N times); mod_php pre-fork behaves like static

success: a request sequence, not a single request, produces the effect — the trigger request and the effect request are different
the effect appears only after a fatal error / OOM / late diagnostic on the producer request
worker-global state (error, session, decoder, extension state) is non-empty at the start of a request that never set it
failure_like: every request starts from provably clean state (instrument the slot before init and find it empty)
the worker exits after the failed startup (PHP-FPM terminates a child when php_request_startup() fails)
the interrupt lands after the matching reset already ran
false_positive: a crash that never crosses a request boundary — a single-request segfault is a DoS, not this record
in-process state reuse that is deliberately per-worker and re-initialised (caches, opcache) — check the slot is actually freed, not recycled
claiming RCE from the crash alone: the vendor is explicit that exploitability needs BOTH a producer and a consumer plus a controllable heap layout

hazards: the two halves are usually in different features — hunt producers and consumers as separate lists and join them last; do not look for one function that does both
session.upload_progress is on by default and needs no session_start(), which is why it is the demonstrated application-independent trigger
with mod_php the producer is .htaccess/php_value config applied before request startup
non_transfers: a one-shot process per request (CGI, per-request container) — no worker, no stale global, no bug
pure managed runtimes that hand each request a fresh isolate (some FaaS); verify the isolate is really fresh before assuming either way
a single-request memory-safety bug that never spans the boundary — that is T-0010, not this
